title: Buddhacarita

attribution.scholarly: Aśvaghoṣa; the Sanskrit survives for cantos 1–14 (to the awakening), the full 28 cantos in Chinese and Tibetan translation

summary: Aśvaghoṣa's epic life of the Buddha. Canto 12 gives the fullest early account of the bodhisattva's teachers: Arāḍa Kālāma expounds a Sāṃkhya-like path — prakṛti and its modifications, the field-knower (kṣetrajña), a five-jointed ignorance (tamas, moha, mahāmoha, tāmisra, andhatāmisra), the four meditations and the sphere of nothingness — which the bodhisattva rejects because a self remains; Udraka teaches neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

editions.name: E. H. Johnston, The Buddhacarita (Lahore 1936), as encoded in the SARIT e-text

notes: Created by U49 for the Arāḍa Kālāma borrowing; the Buddhist units may extend it. Local: SARIT markdown and DCS (catalog:DCS:Buddhacarita).

title: Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (The Mingling of the Two Oceans)

attribution.scholarly: Dārā Shikoh (1655); a Sanskrit rendering, Samudrasaṅgama, is ascribed to his circle

summary: CONTEXT ONLY (Sufism is outside the ontology's scope). Dārā Shikoh sets side by side, topic by topic (elements, senses, the names and attributes of God, the four worlds, the cosmic ages, liberation), the terms of the Sufis and of 'the monotheists of India', holding that the two differ only in wording. Recorded as a document of exchange, not as a source of Sufi doctrine.
notes: Recalled; chapter contents and the Sanskrit version's attribution to be checked in Phase C. No teachings are extracted from it (context only).

title: The dialogues of Bābā Lāl and Dārā Shikoh (Nādir al-nikāt / Mukālama)

attribution.tradition: record of questions put by Dārā Shikoh to the ascetic Bābā Lāl (1653)
attribution.scholarly: Persian record compiled in Dārā's circle; recensions differ

summary: CONTEXT ONLY. Questions on the ascetic life, the guru, the name, the body and liberation put by Dārā Shikoh to a Hindu ascetic of Punjab, recorded in Persian; a document of the Sant–Sufi exchange of the 17th century.
notes: Low confidence on title forms and on Bābā Lāl's affiliation (variously described as a Vaiṣṇava or Kabīr-like ascetic); flagged in REPORT.md for checking. No teachings extracted.

title: Amṛtasiddhimūla
alt_titles: bdud rtsi grub pa'i rtsa ba (Tibetan, Tōh 2285)

attribution.tradition: The Derge colophon (145a.1) reads 'the Amṛtasiddhi composed by the great master Virūpa is complete' and says it was translated by an Indian master, a yogin who had attained siddhi (name read uncertainly)

summary: In the Derge Tengyur (Tōh 2285, among the siddhas' works of vol. zhi) the text opens with homage to Śrī Heruka and to a three-eyed, head-severed, red deity who dispels the fear of death, then announces the 'great seals' (phyag rgya chen po) and teaches the seated seal with the heel at the perineum — the mahāmudrā of the early haṭha texts — in a Buddhist tantric frame.

editions.name: Derge Tengyur Tōh 2285 (Esukhia digital edition), 142b.7–145a.1
editions.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

notes: U49 contribution from the local Derge text; the Sanskrit (ed. Mallinson & Szántó 2021) was not available here.
